# Boiler Spares Knowledge Base — Wickford Plumbing Supplies

Created: 19 Oct 2026 (Europe/London) — first trawl, not exhaustive.
Purpose: help counter / phone staff identify the right boiler spare, find the correct manufacturer part number, and understand what a Gas Safe engineer is likely to need — without diagnosing gas work for DIY fitting.

## How to use this knowledge base

1. Start here for the workflow, then:
2. `brands-and-manuals.md` — where the official manual / spares diagram for that make lives, and how its model / GC / serial numbers work.
3. `fault-diagnosis.md` — symptom first, then brand fault-code system. Use it to narrow to *likely* part(s), not to declare a part faulty.
4. `parts-glossary.md` — what each part does, typical failure symptoms, common confusions (e.g. diverter valve body vs motor vs cartridge).
5. `part-number-identification.md` — the checklist to run before ordering anything.
6. `dhs-and-suppliers.md` — DHS (Direct Heating Spares) lookup, PartsArena, and merchant cross-checks.
7. `forums-and-resources.md` — professional forums / helplines, and their access limits.
8. `model-fault-and-spares-tables.md` — (Round 2) per-model fault tables + spares notes from manuals actually fetched.
9. `testing-values.md` — (Round 2) NTC tables, voltages and resistances stated in those manuals, per model.
10. `dhs-lookup-worked-examples.md` — (Rounds 2-3) ten live DHS appliance lookups with GC, listing numbers and MPNs as displayed.
11. `model-fault-and-spares-tables.md` §11-27 — (Round 3) Vaillant retry, Duo-tec 2/Promax/Main platform, Vogue, Greenstar 2000/8000, Vitodens 050, Alpha NX, Ultimate3, Heatline Monza, Keston Combi 2, Ariston Clas.
12. `legacy-boilers.md` — (Round 3) Suprima, Classic, Junior/CDi, TurboMAX/CombiCompact, CXi legacy identification, obsolete/supersession cautions.
13. `cross-brand-equivalents.xlsx` + `.csv` — (deep pass, Dan's part-number chaining) Verified cross-brand = **19 truly cross-company rows**; separate same-company sheets: Baxi Heating 17 rows, Vaillant Group 6 rows (both NOT cross-brand, not counted); 14 probable. New 'Also listed as / chain' column shows every number matched together per row (diverter motor, diverter valve, flow turbine, pressure sensor, PRV, AAV, NTC, APS chains).
14. `cross-brand-equivalents.md` — method, group/OEM logic, traps (178985 collision, coding plugs, 24V vs 230V valves), counter verification workflow.

## Safety / legal note — read first

- Work on gas appliances, flues, combustion, gas valves, burners and sealed combustion chambers in the UK must be done by a **competent person**; anyone carrying out gas work for payment must be **Gas Safe registered** for that appliance type. Sources: Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 reg.3 — https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1998/2451/regulation/3 ; HSE L56 — https://www.hse.gov.uk/pUbns/priced/l56.pdf ; Gas Safe Register — https://www.gassaferegister.co.uk/
- This knowledge base is for **parts identification and counter advice only**. It does not make a householder competent to open a boiler, and we should not talk a non-registered person through gas-side, flue or combustion repairs.
- Safe customer-level checks we *can* mention are those in the manufacturer's user guide: system pressure (typically re-pressurise to 1–1.5 bar where the user guide says so), condensate pipe frozen outside, gas meter credit / supply on, controls / thermostat calling, reset **once** as the user guide instructs. If it recurs — Gas Safe engineer.
- Use only manufacturer-approved spares. Baxi makes this point explicitly, including liability for copy/refurbished parts: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/spare-parts

## Quick fault-to-part diagnostic workflow

```
1. IDENTIFY THE APPLIANCE EXACTLY
   - Photo of the DATA BADGE / data plate (not just the front logo)
   - Make, full model, output (kW), GC number (format 00-000-00), serial number, fuel (NG/LPG), combi/system/heat-only
   - Front badges lie: a case swapped or a range name (e.g. "Logic") covers many variants.

2. GET THE SYMPTOM IN PLAIN WORDS
   - No heating AND no hot water? Heating only fails? DHW only fails? Intermittent? Noise? Leak? Lockout?
   - When does it happen (from cold, after 10 mins, only on DHW draw-off, in cold weather)?

3. READ THE FAULT CODE EXACTLY AS DISPLAYED
   - Letters matter: F / L / E / EA etc., flashing or solid, any second code alternating.
   - Photograph the display. Note if the code changes after reset.

4. CONFIRM IN THE MANUAL FOR *THAT* MODEL
   - Fault-code tables differ by model/generation within the same brand. Check the
     installation & servicing instructions for that appliance, not a generic blog list.
   - List what the manual says the code means AND its listed causes — most codes have 3-6 causes.

5. ISOLATE BEFORE ORDERING A PART
   - Cheap/external causes first: pressure, air, frozen/blocked condensate, gas supply,
     controls calling, pump running, system sludge/blockage, condensate, flue terminal.
   - Engineer tests (Gas Safe): supply voltages, sensor resistance vs the manual's table,
     fan operation, ignition sequence stage reached.

6. CROSS-CHECK THE PART NUMBER
   - Exploded diagram + position number -> manufacturer part number -> supersessions
   - See part-number-identification.md checklist (voltage, gas type, seals included?, kit contents)

7. ORDER WITH THE FULL ID ON THE NOTE
   - "Make + model + GC + serial + part number + diagram position" on every order/enquiry.
```

### The ignition sequence (why "which stage did it reach?" locates the part)
A modern condensing boiler normally runs: call for heat → pump/fan pre-purge → fan proven (air pressure / fan speed feedback) → ignition spark → gas valve opens → flame detected (rectification/ionisation) → modulation. Where it stops points to the family of parts: no fan = fan/PCB/power; fan runs, no spark = ignition/PCB/ APS on older types; spark, no flame = gas/ignition position/condensate/flue; flame lights then drops = rectification electrode/lead/earth/condensate. This is generic method only — the manual for the model governs.

## Our stock — pending

**No boiler-spares stock list was found on the box on 19 Oct 2026.** I checked `/workspace` (including `stock_existing*.txt`, `price-file-index.md`, `/workspace/intact/`, `/workspace/vaillant/`). What exists is:
- `/workspace/vaillant/sp.pdf` / `sp.txt` — a Vaillant *spare parts catalogue* (ecoTEC plus 824/831/837 etc., doc 0020010870.05 GB 10/2008) — a manufacturer's catalogue, **not** Wickford stock.
- `/workspace/price-file-index.md` — an index of supplier price files on a shared drive, mentioning e.g. an Intergas price list (Sept 2022, marked old) and STC "Baxi January 24.pdf" — not a stockholding list.

**To match "what do we hold" I need one of:**
- An Intact / Xline stock export (CSV or Excel) filtered to boiler spares / heating spares, ideally with: our SKU, description, manufacturer part number, brand, stock qty, location; **or**
- A simple product list / shelf list from the spares bay (photo or spreadsheet).

Once supplied, the parent agent can cross-reference it against the part categories in `parts-glossary.md` and build a "usually-in-stock vs order-in" list. Do not assume any part is in stock until that export is seen.

## Limits of this first trawl
- Prioritises current/common UK domestic combi, system and heat-only boilers and *method* + common faults. Legacy / commercial / oil coverage is signposted, not deep.
- No part number, fault code or resistance value is included unless it came from a fetched official/manual source, cited next to it. Anything else is marked `unverified — check manual`.

files.brands-and-manuals.md:
# Brands & Manuals — verified official sources

Rule: only URLs fetched/verified in research on 19 Oct 2026 are listed as official. If a brand has no public spares catalogue, that is stated — use DHS / PartsArena instead (see `dhs-and-suppliers.md`).

## How numbers generally work (UK)

- **GC (Gas Council) number:** a 7-digit UK appliance identifier usually printed `00-000-00` on the data plate. It identifies the exact appliance variant, not just the range, and is the best single key for spares lookup. Sources: https://www.tradepartsfinder.co.uk/articles/what-is-the-gc-number-on-a-boiler ; https://myboiler.com/what-is-a-gc-number/
- **Manufacturer part number:** the maker's own number for the spare (format is brand-specific — do not guess it). Always quote it with the appliance GC/model.
- **Serial number:** identifies production date/variant. Formats differ by brand and generation — see per-brand notes; if the manual doesn't decode it, record it verbatim and give it to the supplier/manufacturer tech line.
- **Data badge location:** commonly behind/inside the front panel, on the underside, or under a controls flap (Worcester manuals note GC details under the controls cover flap — source: Worcester Greenstar CDi manual via https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/support/literature/download/6720812177/12515 ). Ask the engineer/customer for a photo of the plate itself.

---

## Baxi (BDR Thermea — includes Main & Potterton, see below)
- Manuals (homeowner literature library): https://www.baxi.co.uk/support/literature-library
- Professional literature library: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/help-and-advice/literature-library
- Spares / genuine parts + PartsArena pointer: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/spare-parts
- Error codes (official): https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/technical-support/error-codes
- Verified code examples (official Baxi FAQ https://www.baxi.co.uk/help-and-advice/faqs/what-do-baxi-error-codes-e23-e53-e133-e119-or-e128-mean ): **E119** = low primary water pressure (<0.5 bar on that guidance — re-pressurise ~1–2 bar); **E133** = gas supply interruption / ignition failure / flame not detected; **E110** = primary water / flue overheat. *Always check the list for the exact model — E-codes vary by range.*
- Identification: Baxi ranges are numeric (200/400/600/800, Platinum, Duo-tec etc.) + output. Use GC + serial from data badge; exploded diagrams via PartsArena / approved stockists / DHS.

## Main (Baxi group brand)
- Sold as Baxi-group; manuals/spares via Baxi literature library above and DHS brand "Main Spare Parts" in the DHS Spares Finder: https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/?page=spares-finder
- Fault codes: Main models commonly share Baxi-family E-codes — `unverified for a specific model — check manual` before quoting one.

## Potterton (Baxi group brand)
- Manuals/spares via Baxi literature library above; DHS brand "Potterton Boiler Spares": https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/?page=spares-finder
- Promax etc. user manuals show the same E-code family (E110/E119/E133 above). Model-specific check required.

## Heatline
- No standalone official UK manual library verified in this trawl. DHS hosts Heatline manuals/models page: https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/boiler-manuals/heatline (models listed there include C/Capriz/Compact/Monza/Solaris/Vizo families — as listed by DHS).
- Identification: give DHS the full model + GC; Heatline is a Vaillant Group brand historically — `unverified — check manual / DHS` for spares route per model.

## Vaillant (user said "Valent")
- Installer literature finder (536 documents, filters include "Spare parts manual"): https://professional.vaillant.co.uk/for-installers/literature-finder/
- Homeowner fault-code list: https://www.vaillant.co.uk/service/boiler-fault-codes/
- Verified ecoTEC pro manual fault examples (official PDF https://professional.vaillant.co.uk/downloads/product-manuals/ecotec-pro-1/ecotec-pro-24-28-combi-installation-and-maintenance-instructions-2055535.pdf ): **F.28** unsuccessful ignition (gas supply, condensate blocked, ignition system, ionisation, earthing, electronics listed); **F.29** re-ignition unsuccessful; **F.32** fan fault; **F.75** (homeowner page) = pressure change too low at pump start — causes include pressure <1 bar, air, water pressure sensor, pump, harness. Do not transfer codes between ecoTEC generations without the manual.
- Serial reading: a secondary source (Trust A Part) describes modern Vaillant serials as 28 characters with production year/week in characters 3–6 — `treat as unverified — confirm with Vaillant` for a given appliance: https://www.trustapart.co.uk/how-old-is-my-boiler/
- Spares: original parts only per manual §13.5.1 (same PDF); exploded views in the model's spare parts manual via Literature Finder; also Vaillant Group `spareCHECK` trade app.
- Local file already on box: `/workspace/vaillant/sp.pdf` — Vaillant spare parts catalogue ecoTEC plus 824/831/837, 612–637 (0020010870.05 GB 10/2008), with burner/heat exchanger/casing exploded sections. Old — verify supersessions before ordering from it.

## Glow-worm (Vaillant Group)
- Homeowner literature: https://glow-worm.co.uk/homeowner/repairs-and-servicing/literature/
- Trade hub: https://www.glow-worm.co.uk/trade/
- Legacy (discontinued) ranges page: https://glow-worm.co.uk/trade/products/glow-worm-legacy-products/
- Spares identification: Glow-worm `spareCHECK` (Vaillant Group trade app, exploded views) — Play Store listing verified in search: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.vaillant_group.sparecheck.glo
- Fault codes are Vaillant-family style on many models but tables are model-specific — `check manual`.

## Viessmann (user said "Wiesmann")
- Manuals hub / ViBooks: https://www.viessmann.co.uk/en/support/manuals.html — search ViBooks by serial/article number from the type plate; trade partners get 30,000+ documents (installation/service, technical guides).
- ViBooks direct: https://vibooks.viessmann-climatesolutions.com/GB/en
- Spare Parts App for professionals: https://www.viessmann.co.uk/en/support/spare-parts-app.html (Partner Portal account; enter serial/model/barcode for exploded diagrams).
- Schematics browser: https://schematics.viessmann.com/?country=GB&lang=en
- Identification: Viessmann leans on the **serial number** more than GC for spares — always quote it.

## Ideal (Ideal Heating)
- User guides hub: https://idealtouch.idealboilers.com/user-guides
- Fault-code FAQ (official): https://idealheating.com/support/faqs/boiler-fault-codes
- Verified Logic-family examples (official FAQ + Logic System2 user guide UIN 237665): **F01/F1** low water pressure (1–1.5 bar); **F02/F2** flame loss; **F03/F3** fan fault; **F04/F05** flow/return thermistor; **L01** flow overheat / no water flow; **L02** ignition lockout. Code presentation (F vs L, flashing letters/numbers) varies by Logic generation — check the model guide.
- Boilers: Logic / Logic+ / Logic Max, Vogue, i-mini etc. — range name alone is not enough; need output + GC/serial.

## Keston (Ideal group)
- Product literature (current + discontinued, incl. C/K series, Heat 2, Combi/System): https://keston.co.uk/product-literature
- Note Keston's history of twin-flue / long-flue system boilers — flue parts are less interchangeable; always model + serial.

## Morco
- Manuals (current + obsolete; some technical manuals sign-in): https://morcoproducts.co.uk/manuals/
- Official spares shop: https://morcoproducts.co.uk/boiler-spares/
- Morco serves caravan/park-home water heaters & boilers heavily — confirm the appliance type (it may not be a standard domestic combi).

## Worcester Bosch
- Literature search: https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/support/literature
- Spare parts (spares catalogue site, 10,000+ parts enquiry system): https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/products/spare-parts
- Fault Finder in Worcester professional app: https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/installers-choice/trade-tips/fault-finder
- Verified Greenstar CDi examples (official manual): **EA** flame not detected (check gas supply, condensate blocked/frozen, flue blocked, then reset); **C6** fan speed too low; **E9** safety temp limiter tripped; **F7/FA** flame detected when it shouldn't be; **b1** code plug not detected. FD number = Worcester factory-date code (secondary source: https://www.trustapart.co.uk/how-old-is-my-boiler/ — `confirm per model`).
- Identification: model + GC under controls flap (per manual) + FD/serial.

## Alpha
- Instruction & user manuals: https://www.alpha-innovation.co.uk/brochures-and-manuals/instruction-and-user-manuals

## Ariston
- UK installation manuals are published per model (e.g. E-Combi ONE manual PDF via ariston.com, found in search). No central library URL verified in this trawl — search Ariston UK by exact model, or use DHS brand selector.

## Ferroli
- Technical documentation (installer toolbox): https://www.ferroli.com/uk/installers/toolbox/documentation

## Intergas
- Downloads (installation, service, parameters): https://intergasstore.co.uk/downloads
- Note: Intergas designs often have fewer moving parts (e.g. no diverter valve on some models — heat exchanger does both duties). `Verify per model in its manual` before assuming a diverter fault is possible.

## Vokera (Vokèra)
- Manuals & literature (includes GC numbers per model): https://www.vokera.co.uk/trade-professionals/manuals-literature/

## Ravenheat / Biasi
- No official UK library verified in this trawl. Route: DHS Spares Finder brand list includes Ravenheat (verified on DHS homepage brand list https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/ ) and Biasi appears in DHS brand list as "Biasi". Use exact model + GC via DHS; mark any other web source `unverified`.

## Vaillant Group note
Vaillant, Glow-worm (and historically Heatline) sit in Vaillant Group UK; Baxi/Main/Potterton sit in BDR Thermea; Ideal/Keston in Groupe Atlantic / Ideal group. Group family explains shared fault-code *style* and parts-binning, but **never** assume a part is interchangeable across brands without the part number cross-check.

# Cross-Brand Equivalents — method, traps, counter verification

> **Correction (19 Oct 2026, per Dan): Baxi, Main and Potterton are the SAME company (Baxi Heating, BDR Thermea). They are NOT separate cross-brand entities.** All Baxi/Main/Potterton same-number rows have been removed from the Verified cross-brand sheet/count and moved to a separate sheet: **'Same company — Baxi Heating (Baxi / Main / Potterton) — NOT cross-brand'** (17 rows). That information is still useful at the counter (one bin serves the three badges), but it is never counted or presented as cross-brand.
> **Second correction (19 Oct 2026, per Dan): Vaillant, Glow-worm and Saunier Duval are the SAME company — Vaillant Group — so they are NOT cross-brand either.** All 4 Vaillant-group rows have been moved off the Verified cross-brand sheet to their own sheet: **'Same company — Vaillant Group (Vaillant / Glow-worm / Saunier Duval) — NOT cross-brand'**.
> **Exhaustive family sweep (19 Oct 2026, night): Verified cross-brand is 27 (was 19)**. Same-company: Baxi Heating 17, Vaillant Group 9, Other groups 2 (Riello group; Ariston/Chaffoteaux/Ecoflam). Probable: 75. A new **Coverage** sheet (also exported as cross-brand-coverage.csv) records, for each family, the seeds tried, chains found, brands with no equivalence and blocked sources. Consistency fix: 14 rows that rested on one retailer's page were moved from Verified to Probable, in line with Dan's rule. Older text below this line describes the earlier passes.

> **Deep pass (19 Oct 2026, Dan's part-number chaining method):** Verified cross-brand sheet = **19 rows, all truly cross-company** (+5 AAV rows this pass, see AAV section below; Vaillant same-company sheet now 6, Probable 14). New chained rows: Elbi/Bitron diverter motor (7216534=997147=BI1101102=0020118640=…), diaphragm diverter valve complete (998069=BI1011503=500601=0020025277), Fugas/Chunhui flow turbine (65100541=JJJ000619050=BI1271501), water pressure sensor (0020059717=87186510420, moved up from Vaillant sheet because the chain spans Bosch), Caleffi PRV (190751=87161424160=075248), AAV (87161064450=176457/Grundfos 59200320), NTC 10027351, Huba APS 65100716. Same-company sheets (not counted): Baxi Heating 17 rows, Vaillant Group 5 rows (fan + flow sensor added; pressure sensor moved out to Verified because its chain spans companies). Probable sheet = 12 rows. A new **'Also listed as / chain'** column in the spreadsheet shows every number matched together per row.

Companion to `cross-brand-equivalents.xlsx` / `.csv`. Fetched 19 Oct 2026. Every Verified row has an evidence URL that was actually fetched in this task (or in rounds 1-3, where stated). Prices/stock never copied — re-check live.

## How the same part ends up with different numbers (3 routes)

### A) Corporate groups share platforms
- **Baxi Heating (Baxi / Main / Potterton / Remeha) — SAME COMPANY, not cross-brand:** Heating Spare Parts' part-number pages list *the same manufacturer code* under the company's badges for sensors (720747101, 720789201), diverter motor (7216534), cartridge (7656807), plate (7223558), pressure switch (5114748), 8L vessel (5114691), PRV (248056), AAV (248043), electrodes (720767301/720767101), gasket (5114755), SIT gas valve kit (720301001), Suprima PCB kit (5111603). This is same-company platform sharing — all 17 such rows live on the 'Same company — Baxi Heating' sheet and are excluded from cross-brand counts. Platform sharing is *selective*, not total — see traps.
- **Vaillant Group (Vaillant / Glow-worm / Saunier Duval / Protherm) — SAME COMPANY (Vaillant Group), not cross-brand:** different *numbers* for the same component is the pattern here — pressure sensor Vaillant 0020059717 = Glow-worm 0020014190/0020079644 = Saunier S5720500/0020023216. Saunier-numbered parts appear on Glow-worm DHS appliance pages (PRV 0020047005, sensor S5720500 on CXi). All 4 such rows live on the 'Same company — Vaillant Group' sheet and are excluded from cross-brand counts — exactly as for Baxi Heating.
- **Ideal Group (Ideal / Keston):** shared *test data* verified (identical thermistor tables in both manuals) — but that does not prove the physical part number is shared; that row sits in Probable.
- **Bosch (Worcester), Ariston, Ferroli, Alpha, Intergas:** cross-brand sharing mostly appears via OEM components (route B) rather than group part-number systems in the sources fetched. Intergas Xclusive/HRE evidence this task was within-brand only. Atlantic/Intergas grouping: `no cross-brand part evidence fetched — do not claim`.

### B) Common OEM makers inside many brands
- **Grundfos-pattern pumps:** one compatible DUCA 15-60 unit is retailer-cross-listed against 30+ brand numbers (Worcester 8716…, Vaillant 1609…/0020136638, Glow-worm, Ideal 175…, Baxi 248042, Vokera, Ariston). Useful — but it's a *compatible*, not proven-genuine, route.
- **Honeywell/Resideo gas valves:** VK4105G (Ideal 075432 = Baxi Heating 245341 — truly cross-company, Ideal vs Baxi Heating) is verified cross-company. VK4105M5108 (5107339) is only evidenced across Baxi Heating's own badges/models, so it moved to the Same-company sheet. The OEM VK code is the real identity; brand number is a label on it.
- **SIT:** 848 Sigma kit as Baxi Heating 720301001 (same-company sheet, not cross-brand evidence).
- **Zilmet-pattern vessels:** compatible 8L/4L units cross-listed against Bosch, Ariston, Ferroli, Ideal, Vaillant numbers (Worimex). Shape and connection rule, not litres alone.
- Not evidenced this task (searched, no fetched tie to specific brand numbers): Giannoni/Sermeta heat exchangers, FIME/ebm-papst fans (search-level only — in Probable), Bertelli, Caleffi as named maker for 248056 (retailer page doesn't state maker — left blank in sheet), Elbi. They stay out of Verified.

### C) Supersessions printed on the listing
- Baxi SIT valve 5119647 → **720301001** (DHS 'has been replaced by', old part discontinued).
- Glow-worm disconnector 801673 → **2000802600 filling loop** (function itself changed).
- Suprima PCB kit 5111603 replaces 5102160/407750/238091 (retailer listing).
- DHS product titles carry 'NOW USE …' — always read the whole title (round-3 CXi lesson).

## Group audit of the remaining 4 verified rows (checked for hidden same-group pairings)
- **Pump head (universal compatible):** its fit list spans Bosch, Ideal Group, Vaillant Group, Baxi Heating, Ariston, Ferroli etc. — cross-company rests on that span. Pairs *inside* the list that are same-group (Vaillant vs Glow-worm; Bosch vs Buderus) are not themselves the claim.
- **Honeywell VK4105G:** Ideal (Ideal Group) ↔ Baxi Heating — different groups. Clean.
- **Zilmet 8L vessel:** Bosch vs Buderus inside the list are one group (Bosch) and are not counted as cross; the row is cross-company because it also spans Ariston, Ferroli and Ideal Group. Annotated in the sheet.
- **Zilmet 4L vessel:** Vaillant vs Protherm inside the list are one group (Vaillant Group) and are not counted as cross; the row is cross-company because it also spans Ferroli, Riello, Hermann, Unical. Annotated in the sheet.
- Probable sheet audited too: CXi PCB/interface rows labelled Vaillant Group same-company; Ideal/Keston row labelled Ideal Group same-group; Baxi 720788001 row labelled Baxi Heating internal; Intergas rows are within-brand conflicts, not cross-brand.

## The big traps (all found in real sources this task / rounds 1-3)

1. **Same number, different part (brand collision): 178985** is a Vaillant 3-bar PRV **and** an Ideal front door panel assembly (both fetched on Heating Spare Parts). A bare number without brand is meaningless.
2. **Same number, conflicting description: 720788001** — Duo-tec 2 manual calls it a Hall effect sensor; the retailer lists it as a drain tap under all three Baxi-group brands. One of them is wrong; do not sell by number until PartsArena/photo confirms.
3. **Coding/R.D.S. and output coding:** Duo-tec 2 R.D.S. units are output+fuel specific (720843201-5301) and fitting one triggers code 55 (calibration). Vaillant DSN/coding resistor (F.70/F.92) — a PCB that 'fits' can still be wrong for the appliance.
4. **24V vs 230V gas valves:** Ideal Logic gas valve is a 24V kit (179032, 24Vdc test); Vokera/Viessmann gas trains are 230Vac. VK model suffixes (VK4105G**1005** vs **1179**, M**5108** vs M**5033** in retailer listings) are different valves wearing one family name.
5. **Diverter trio:** motor (7216534) / cartridge (7656807) / complete valve (7224764-type) — three orders, one symptom. And platform sharing is selective: flow sensor 720747101 is shared Baxi↔Main, diverter motor in Duo-tec 2's manual (720788601) differs from Main's (7216534) while DHS fits 7216534 to Duo-Tec 2 — serial/output check, not faith.
6. **Build-date splits:** Vaillant ecoTEC control box to/from 08-09/07; CombiCompact water valve to/from 04/95; Suprima/Duo Tec fits lists with BEFORE/AFTER serials; Intergas ignition module manual 801477 vs DHS 801537 (unresolved — Probable sheet).
7. **Ratings are model property:** PRV 3 bar (Baxi 248056) vs 3.5 bar (Glow-worm Betacom 0020061610); vessel 8L vs 10L, flat vs round, 3/8 vs M14; plate HEX by plate count/kW.
8. **Seals & kit contents:** combustion gasket 5114755 is itself a shared part — if you sell the shared fan/burner without the shared gasket, the job still fails. Check 'kit' contents (SIT 848 *kit* vs bare valve).
9. **Compatible ≠ genuine:** DUCA pump and Worimex vessels are compatible-pattern parts. For gas/combustion parts, genuine route is the default (Baxi liability note, round 1); compatibles must be sold as compatibles.

## Counter verification workflow (before selling anything as 'equivalent')
```
1. Brand + model + GC + serial from data badge (photo). No badge = no equivalence sale.
2. Find the part on the APPLIANCE's diagram/list first (DHS appliance page / PartsArena / manual short list).
3. Only then cross: does an evidence source (sheet row) tie THAT number to the other brand/number?
   - Same group number under 2+ brands (Heating Spare Parts pattern) = strongest.
   - Different numbers, one retailer cross-list (e.g. a same-group sensor pattern on the same-company sheets) = check plug/thread/photo on both listings; and first check the two brands are actually different companies (see sheet names).
   - OEM code match (VK…, SIT 848) = match the FULL suffix, not the family.
4. Check the trap list: voltage, rating (bar/L/plates), output/fuel, build date, coding device, seals included.
5. Write both numbers on the order ('supplied as X, equivalent to Y per [source]') so returns/credit are traceable.
6. If sources conflict (Intergas ignition, 720788001) — stop, phone manufacturer/DHS. Conflict is data, not a tie-break vote.
```


## Deep pass — Dan's part-number chaining (19 Oct 2026, evening)

Method, exactly as instructed: pick a seed part/number, fetch its product page, harvest **every** alternative/cross-reference/superseded number on that page, search those numbers, harvest the next page, and match the chain together. A row is Verified only where a page explicitly lists the numbers as alternatives for the same part (ideally two independent pages); single-page chains sit in Probable.

### Seeds worked, by family (honest result per family)
- **Diverter motors/actuators — WORKED, big chain found.** Seed: Glow-worm 0020118640 'Diverter Valve Motor 3WV ELBI' (Heating Spare Parts) → Elbi/Bitron motor → Fausto Elbi page (Ariston 997147, Saunier S5720600, Savio BI1351108/1101102, Riello 4365774/4364657, Chaffoteaux 61302483-01, Immergas 1.018064) → Euro DV.550/DV.551 (adds Baxi 7216534/248733/5132452/710188301, Glow 0020061621, Ideal 174813 on DV.551 only) → Worimex Chunhui motor page confirms Ariston/Riello/Biasi/Saunier subset. **This is the diverter motor Dan said was cross-branded — he was right.** TrustAPart's universal Elbi/Bitron actuator (220-240V) independently lists Alpha/Ariston/Biasi/Remeha/Glow-worm/Halstead/Heatline/Ravenheat/Ideal/Saunier/Vokera fits.
- **Diverter valves/cartridges/bodies — WORKED.** Complete diaphragm valve DV.650 chain (Ariston 998069/573121 = Biasi BI1011503 = Halstead 500601 = Protherm 0020025277/S93440070, also-fit Ideal CF80) confirmed on two pages (Euro + TradeBoilerParts, diaphragm BI1011103). Cartridge kit 44-BX-12 (Baxi/Ariston/Biasi title claim) is **Probable** — the fetched YourSpares page supports Baxi only.
- **Flow turbines/sensors — WORKED, with a negative result Dan asked to see.** Seed (Dan's example): Ideal flow turbine. Ideal 176473 = Grundfos 59200311, ABK-prefix onwards; earlier cartridges 175660/175661/175662 (8/12L variants) + sensor 175590. Chasing 59200311 found **no other brand's number** — that Grundfos kit is Ideal-only in every fetched listing, so no cross-brand row was made from it (forcing one would be invention). The cross-company flow chain came from the other direction: Worimex 'Flow Turbine Chunhui' + Ziperone Fugas pages match **Ariston 65100541 = Baxi JJJ000619050/619050 = Biasi BI1271501**. Vaillant ecoFIT flow sensor 0020211945=0020197555=0020213122 is Vaillant-Group-internal (same-company sheet).
- **Fans — chained, no cross-company chain found.** FIME GR01855N = Vaillant 0020020008 (Protherm 0020213171 — same group, moved to Vaillant sheet). Every other fan chain (Baxi Solo FA.180/182, Vaillant FA.151) stayed inside one brand. Do not sell fans cross-brand on wattage.

- **Pressure sensors/switches — WORKED.** Vaillant 0020059717 chain extended to Worcester 87186510420 (TrustAPart, two product pages) — row **moved from the Vaillant same-company sheet to Verified**, with the Glow-worm/Saunier links annotated as same-group inside. Huba APS 65/50 Pa: Ariston 65100716 (now 65104671-01) cross-listed for Baxi/Westen/Beretta by Ziperone + Worimex.

### Ideal ↔ Baxi flow turbines — Dan's screenshot claim, tested (19 Oct 2026, late)

**Verdict in plain terms: Dan is substantially right, with one precision.** The Ideal and Baxi brass cartridges in the screenshot are the **same Fugas turbine-cartridge family** — same brass cartridge form, same job (spin a turbine, Hall sensor 175590-type reads it, boiler sees DHW demand). What differs between the numbers is the **flow rating**, which tracks boiler size. So it is category **(b) same body/cartridge family, different rating variant** — not (a) one identical part under two numbers, and not (c) look-alike. A rating-matched cartridge is the cross-brand buy; a wrong-rating one will physically go in but give wrong DHW flow/switching.

**What sets the rating:** the flow regulator/restrictor inside the cartridge housing. Ideal's own Logic manual states it twice: performance table footnote '** In areas of low water pressure the DHW restrictor can be removed' and servicing Frame 66 'the domestic hot water regulator may be removed from the DHW flow turbine cartridge' (manual fetched: downloads.ctfassets.net Ideal Logic Combi Installation & Servicing). No Fugas datasheet/K-factor was found — that mechanism is manual evidence, not an OEM spec sheet, and is recorded as such.

**Ideal range fetched:** 175660 HE24 Fugas 10391 (8L, Logic 24); 175661 HE30 Fugas 10393 (12L per UK retailer + compatible maker); 175662 HE35 Fugas 10394 (12L UK / '10LT' Turkish compatible maker — **conflict, see Probable**); 176139 HE38 Fugas 10.0457; 176876 40kW Vogue ref 10.0575; 176473 ABK-onwards Grundfos 59200311 kit (different system, no Baxi pairing).
**Baxi Heating range fetched:** 7663533 10L (Main Eco Compact 25/Potterton 25); 7663535 12L (Baxi 624/630/825/830, and via inlet 5114710 Duo-tec/Platinum per another retailer — fit lists differ, check GC); 7798983 12L (Duo-tec 2/EcoBlue, DHS); 711633500 → 767486000 10L; 7211822 12L 'flow regulator'.

**Pairings added to the sheet:** Verified — 12L: Ideal 175661/175662 ↔ Baxi 7663535/7798983; Verified (weaker, compatible-maker evidence, no Baxi genuine number) — 8L: Ideal 175660 sold as 'Baxi and Ideal compatible' at 8LT. Probable — 10L pairing, blocked by the 175662 rating conflict. Every turbine row carries 'match the litres/min rating to boiler size'.

**Regulator ≠ turbine cartridge (task 5):** do not conflate them. On ABK-onwards Logic the diagram lists them as separate items: 176470 flow regulator (Grundfos 59200313, item 124) vs 176473 flow sensor/turbine kit (59200311, item 127). On the older Fugas boilers the regulator is an insert *inside* the turbine-cartridge housing (removable per the manual), which is exactly why retailers muddle the names: Baxi 7211822 is called 'Flow Regulator 12L' by Spares-Direct (spring-loaded insert), 'Flow Turbine Cartridge' by Aspares (jointly with 7663535), and appears inside Worimex's turbine chain for JJJ000619050. Same housing, two functions, listings disagree — check the diagram position, not the retailer's title.

### Conflicts/traps found in this pass
- Euro lists **two** diverter-motor codes, DV.550 and DV.551, with overlapping but different number sets — DV.551 adds Ideal 174813 and Glow 0020118640. The 174813 leg is retailer-compatible only; Ideal's newer diverter motor 181018 is a **24V Minebea** kit — a different motor. Voltage (24V vs 220-240V) is the trap inside Dan's own diverter family.
- Worimex flow page lists Baxi 7211822 in the turbine chain, but 7211822 also appears as a Baxi **flow regulator** — description conflict, flagged in the sheet; verify on the appliance diagram.
- SIT gas-valve family names (848/845) hide different codes/coil colours/voltages — never cross on 'SIT 848' alone.
- Same bare number, shared sensor: 10027351 works cross-brand **only** where the manual's resistance curve matches (flue NTCs are often a different curve).


## AAVs / automatic air vents — Dan's hunch, tested (19 Oct 2026, late)

**You were right again: boiler AAVs are heavily cross-branded, and the reason is simple — most of them are standard Caleffi vents in brand packaging.** TradeBoilerParts literally sells the genuine Baxi vent headed 'Baxi 248043 — AAV Original Caleffi Part'. These are boiler-internal automatic air vents (pump manifold / vent body inside the boiler), **not** plumbing Durgo/soil air-admittance valves. Where the boiler part is just a standard heating vent, the rows say so (category c).

**OEM logic:** Caleffi dominates (MINICAL 5020 series: 502030 = 3/8" G, 502040 = 1/2" G, per Caleffi's official page; ROBOCAL/Slimline 5026-type; multifit vent heads). Grundfos/Wilo plastic pump bodies take screw-on vent heads (Euro AV.235/AV.235S). Flamco/Spirotech/Taco/Honeywell: searched, **no fetched tie to a UK boiler brand number** — they stay out of the sheet.

**Chains now on the sheet (all with the thread/form recorded):**
- **AV.250 complete vent (existing row, deepened):** Worcester 87161064450 = Ideal 176457 (Grundfos 59200320) = Ferroli 39818220 = Viessmann 7828750 = Alpha 1.027110 = Baxi 720777601.
- **AV.235 Caleffi HEAD (new):** one screw-on head lists Vaillant 104521→0010033857, Biasi BI1212107, Viessmann 7828557, Vokera 10025485/20035019, Alpha 1.022102, Ideal 174894, Ariston 65104703 (+ Vaillant-group Glow/Saunier/Heatline numbers inside). Category (b): same head, pump body differs.
- **AV.230 Caleffi HEAD (new):** Baxi 248043 (→5114706 complete vent) = Glow/Saunier S1005600/2000801898 = Sime 6013101.
- **AV.170 complete vent (new):** Alpha 1.010771 = Baxi 5130570/Potterton 5122330 (+ Grant MPCBS29 on a compatible listing).
- **AV.110 complete vent, 3/8" (new):** Worcester 87161405000 = Vaillant 061707 = Ideal 075452 = a bog-standard Caleffi 502030. Category (c) in its purest form.
- **AV.250B (new):** Baxi 720777601 = Ideal 175804 (two retailers) — **conflicts** with AV.250's Baxi leg (same Baxi number claimed for both Euro products); flagged in both rows, photo-match before selling.
- **Same-company Vaillant row added:** Vaillant 104521→0010033857 = Glow-worm 0020014161 = Saunier S1024500 (City Plumbing UCP page lists all three for one vent) — same group, not counted. The cross-company action for that vent is at head level (AV.235 via Biasi).
- **Intergas:** their HRE vent 843017 is a **manual** 3/8" air-release valve, not an automatic vent — a standard 3/8" automatic vent is the functional equivalent thread-wise, but no Intergas automatic-vent brand number was found to chain. Recorded here, no row invented.

**Thread/form traps (the whole game with AAVs):**
1. **3/8" vs 1/2":** Caleffi 502030 (3/8") and 502040 (1/2") look alike; Euro AV.110 (3/8") vs AV.120 (1/2", Ravenheat 5015015) vs AV.130 Slimline (3/8") are three different orders. Measure the tapping, not the silhouette.
2. **Head vs complete vent:** AV.235/AV.230/AV.220V are heads that screw onto an existing pump/vent body. A complete-vent number (248043, 104521) will not be fixed by a head if the body/float has failed — and a head is a fraction of the price, so this mistake is common and annoying.
3. **Head length:** AV.235S is a SHORT Grundfos/Wilo multifit head for 0010033857 — same family, different length.
4. **Same brand, different vent:** Ideal 175804 ≠ 176457 ≠ 174894 — three different Ideal vents. Worcester 87161064450 ≠ 87161405000 (complete vs 3/8" CDi-era). One brand badge proves nothing.
5. **Check/shut-off arrangement:** whether there's an isolating cap/check valve under the vent varies by boiler — if the old vent sits on a check fitting, a bare threaded vent changes how the engineer can service it. Compare the whole stack, not just the vent.

## Exhaustive family sweep — 14 families (19 Oct 2026, night)

**Group updates applied:** Riello / Beretta / Vokera / Sylber joined **Ariston Group on 1 Jul 2026** (Riello press release), so Vokera↔Ariston/Chaffoteaux is now same-group. **Alpha is Immergas Group** (Immergas has owned 100% since 2000). Ideal/Keston have been part of **Groupe Atlantic** since 2015. Biasi (Belloni family) and Sime are independent. Remeha/De Dietrich are BDR Thermea (Baxi's parent).

**Rule tightened:** Verified now means the brand↔brand link appears on **at least two independent sites**, or on one site plus a page that ties it to the same OEM code. A link on one retailer only (almost always Euro Boiler Parts) goes to Probable, labelled "explicit cross-listing on ONE retailer only".

| Family | New verified | Highlights | No cross-company found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 PRVs | 0 (SV.130 kept) | Vokera 1806→2907 = Beretta R2907 = Riello 4365230 (same group); SV.110 multifit, SV.310 Worcester=Glow-worm, SV.160 Vaillant=Worcester, SV.421 Vokera=Glow-worm, SV.150/155/420/500/530 → Probable | Ravenheat SV.510, Alpha 1.023565, Ariston 573172 |
| 2 Diverters | 0 (Elbi row deepened) | **Elbi OEM code 31650047** confirmed (Fausto Ricambi) + Ferroli 39842120, Fagor, Roca, Beretta R10025304; Ariston 65104314 cartridge = Chaffoteaux/Ecoflam (same group) | **Ideal 24V Minebea 181018 is NOT the Elbi 230V motor**; Vaillant SAIA 178978 |
| 3 Flow | +2 | Ideal 172503 = Biasi BI1091104; Bosch 87186456840 = Biasi BI1441501 (Bitron 20490948); Chunhui turbine row gains Baxi 7211822 + Remeha; Protherm 0020035580 = Baxi 7798983 (Probable) | Ferroli Eltek, Vaillant 178988 |
| 4 Pumps | 0 | Biasi BI1262103 = Ideal Mini 173778 (Probable, Euro only); UPM3 Baxi/Ideal/Vaillant = same family, not proven same part (PWM profile) | Vaillant, Alpha |

| 7 NTCs | 0 | TS.131 Alpha 1.021762 = Baxi 5108265 = Vokera 7022 (Probable); **curve not stated anywhere** | Ideal 175594 |
| 8 APS | 0 | 4 Euro-only chains (Alpha=Baxi C6065F1100; Ravenheat=Saunier Huba 49/34 Pa; Ravenheat=Biasi; Alpha=Sime) → Probable | most single-brand |
| 9 Gas valves | +2 | **SIT 0.845.057**: Ideal 172611/173220 = Biasi BI1093104 = Ariston 65100516 = Vokera 10025074 = Heatline D003200419; **VK4105C1017**: Ferroli 39820600 = Sime 6243815 = Halstead 500569 | Vaillant VK8x15, Worcester VR4601 |
| 10 Plate HEX | 0 | Zilmet 14/16-plate Biasi/Ideal/Glow-worm/Ariston, Alfa Laval Ariston/Heatline/Halstead → Probable (Euro only, dimensions given) | Vaillant, Worcester, Baxi |

| 14 PCBs | +1 | Ideal 172548 = Biasi BI1305101 ignition PCB (4 sites) | all main PCBs |

**Pattern:** most of the new verified links run **Ideal ↔ Biasi**. The Ideal Mini/Europa/Icon were Biasi-built, and Ideal sells several parts under the Biasi number. The second big tie is the **OEM code** (SIT 845, Honeywell VK41xx, Elbi 31650047, Zilmet, Chunhui/Bitron). Match on that code plus suffix, not on the brand number alone.

**Conflicts recorded (not smoothed over):** Glow-worm 2000801904 on two different PRVs (SV.421 female vs SV.180 male); Ideal 175551 described as both 8L and 10L; Ariston 990685 with 142mm vs 147mm lugs; Sime Format HE on two Honeywell valves; FSC.460 adds Ideal 175660 (8L) to the BI1271501 chain; Euro titles that carry numbers missing from the description (TS.131, AP.109, HE.251, PC.130/610).

**Gaps / blocked:** Worimex product pages need JavaScript (title evidence only); Euro category URLs are mislabelled (e.g. 'temperature-sensors-thermistors-25-c' = low water sensors; 'diverter-valves-motors-cartridges-13-c' = pumps); only the first page of each Euro PCB subcategory was scanned; Watts/Giacomini/RWC/Comap/Sauter/Trafag/Danfoss/Bertelli/ebm-papst/FIME numbers never appeared on boiler cross-lists; Intergas/Morco not reached. Next best step: find second independent pages for the ~45 'ONE retailer' Probable rows. Many would then move up.

## Sources that worked (honest ranking)
- **Heating Spare Parts part-number pages** — best for Baxi Heating same-company identification: one URL explicitly lists the same code under each of the company's badges with GC fits. Useful, but by Dan's correction it is not cross-brand evidence. Pattern: heatingspareparts.com/boiler-spares/partno/<number>.
- **DHS product pages** — best for supersessions ('NOW USE', discontinued notices) and 'This Part Fits' appliance lists; DHS appliance pages surface cross-brand listings (Saunier parts on Glow-worm, Potterton cartridge on Baxi).
- **Retailer compatible cross-lists** (Capital Boiler Parts pump, Euro Boiler Parts Honeywell, Worimex Zilmet, Altoe sensor) — best for OEM route, but they sell compatibles: confidence is in the *fit list*, not in genuine identity.
- **Manufacturer manuals** (rounds 2-3 short parts lists) — ground truth for what the brand itself codes the part; the cross happens when two brands' manuals print the same number (720747101).
- **PartsArena** — account-gated; not directly fetched this task. Use it as the in-shop diagram check (step 2), not as citable evidence here.

## Gaps
No fetched evidence tying: Giannoni/Sermeta exchangers to brand numbers, Elbi vessels, Bertelli components, Worcester↔Bosch (Buderus) UK cross-numbers, Ariston-group (Chaffoteux) UK numbers beyond Worimex compatible list, Ferroli OEM suppliers, Alpha OEM suppliers. Fan OEM cross (ebm-papst/FIME) is search-level only (Probable). Those need OEM catalogues / a PartsArena session — round 4 candidates.
Stock note: nothing here says Wickford holds any of these — Intact export still pending.

## Gap passes A/B + final audit (19 Oct 2026)
Counts: Verified 33 · Vaillant Group 16 · Baxi Heating 18 · Other groups 4 · Probable 67.

# DHS & Suppliers — verified routes to the right part

## DHS — Direct Heating Spares (https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/)
Verified 19 Oct 2026 via homepage, Spares Finder and FAQ (https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/frequently-asked-questions).

- **What it is:** UK spares specialist (Chorley, Lancashire, trading since 2006 per FAQ), says 20,000+ spares in stock, next-day delivery available, 7pm order cut-off claimed on homepage.
- **Lookup works three ways (per FAQ):**
  1. **Part number** in the search box — "easiest way if you have a part number".
  2. **Spares Finder / appliance selector** (https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/?page=spares-finder): Brand → Appliance → Category → Sub-category → Part. Brand list verified includes Baxi, Potterton, Main, Vaillant, Glowworm, Ideal Domestic, Keston, Morco, Heatline, Viessmann, Intergas, Alpha, Ariston, Ferroli, Vokera, Ravenheat, Biasi and many more.
  3. Phone **0330 123 3707** / live chat (7 days a week per FAQ) if model/GC not found.
- **GC-number pages:** appliance pages state the GC number and list parts that fit that appliance — verified example: Ideal Classic FF 350 page gives "GC Number: 41-391-96" and lists parts with manufacturer part numbers (e.g. Ideal 171461 Fan Assembly Kit) — https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/category/gas-boiler-uk/brand/ideal-domestic/appliance/ideal-classic-ff-350-ide226 . *Prices/stock on that page are live data — never copy them into notes; check at order time.*
- **Categories** used by DHS (useful as a checklist of part families): Air Pressure Switch, Auto Air Vent, Burner, Condensate Trap, Diverter Valve, Electrodes, Expansion Vessels, Fans, Flow Switch, Flue, Gas Valves, Heat Exchanger, Ignition Unit, Orings/Washers/Gaskets, Printed Circuit Board, Pumps, Pressure Relief & Safety Valves, Thermistor… full list: https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/category/gas-boiler-uk
- **Manuals:** DHS also hosts free boiler manual downloads by brand (e.g. Heatline page https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/boiler-manuals/heatline) — cross-check against the manufacturer library where one exists.
- **Accounts/pricing:** FAQ states you do **not** need an account to buy; DHS sells to trade and general public; trade credit account available by application; **for trade prices, phone** — website prices shown inc VAT on retail pages. So: Wickford's DHS terms/pricing depend on our own trade account/login — `confirm our account terms before quoting margins`. Trade counter (Chorley) prices may differ from website (per FAQ).
- **Genuine vs alternative:** DHS sells "brand new genuine", "alternative/similar" and "refurbished/tested" options, labelled on product pages (FAQ). For gas-carrying / combustion parts, prefer genuine manufacturer parts and say so (see Baxi genuine-parts liability note in README).

## PartsArena (Wolseley)
- Manufacturer-backed parts-identification database (Baxi directs users to it: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/spare-parts).
- How it works (Wolseley guide / PartsArena): search manufacturer, model, GC number, part number or keyword → interactive exploded diagram → tap position hotspot → part description, photo, manufacturer/stockist codes → basket/share. Source: https://www.wolseley.co.uk/wcsstore/Wolseley/Attachment/how-to-guides/how-to-guide-parts-arena-mobile.pdf ; https://www.partsarena.com/partsarena-pro-for-field-engineers/
- Access: aimed at Wolseley trade account holders / heating professionals; PartsArena Pro app adds offline use, manuals & barcode scanning. If Wickford has a Wolseley account, this is the fastest diagram route for Baxi-group and many other brands.

## Manufacturer spares routes (cross-check source of truth)
- Baxi Genuine Parts via approved stockists / PartsArena (above).
- Vaillant / Glow-worm: spare parts manual per model in Literature Finder https://professional.vaillant.co.uk/for-installers/literature-finder/ ; `spareCHECK` trade apps.
- Viessmann Spare Parts App (Partner Portal login; serial-number driven exploded views): https://www.viessmann.co.uk/en/support/spare-parts-app.html
- Worcester Bosch Spares catalogue site (10,000+ parts, build an enquiry to share with a stockist): https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/products/spare-parts
- Morco direct spares shop: https://morcoproducts.co.uk/boiler-spares/

## Merchant / trade-counter alternatives
- **City Plumbing — Spares Finder:** says 20,000+ identifiable parts, branch Click & Collect / delivery: https://www.cityplumbing.co.uk/c/product/spares/c/1827000/ and https://www.cityplumbing.co.uk/content/spares-finder-info
- **Wolseley / Plumb Centre:** boiler parts via branches + PartsArena (above): https://www.wolseley.co.uk/
- **Screwfix / Plumbase:** `not verified in this trawl` — Screwfix is strong on controls/programmers/thermostats and generic heating parts, weaker on model-specific boiler internals; check at need rather than assuming a gas-side spare is stocked.
- General rule: manufacturer list/DHS/PartsArena to *identify*, then merchant/DHS to *source* — never identify from a retailer's keyword listing alone.

## Wickford-specific unknowns (to confirm internally)
- Do we hold a DHS trade credit account, a Wolseley/PartsArena login, City Plumbing trade account? What are our carriage/cut-off terms with each? None of this is on the box — ask Dan / check Intact supplier records before this file is treated as ordering procedure.

3. Sub-parts (motor/cartridge/body; sensor/adaptor) sit adjacent — diagram number + MPN both go on the order.
4. Where manual and DHS numbers conflict (Intergas ignition), stop and phone.

# Fault Diagnosis — symptom first, then brand codes

How to use: (1) match the plain-English symptom, work the "checks before replacing" column; (2) then match the brand code in the model's own manual. **A code lists causes, not a verdict.** Codes below are only those verified from official sources in this trawl (see `brands-and-manuals.md` for citations) — for any other code: `check manual`.

## By generic symptom

### No heating AND no hot water
- Checks first: power/display on? Pressure ~1–1.5 bar cold? Controls calling (room stat, timer, receiver)? Fault code shown? Frozen condensate in cold snap? Gas supply on / meter credit?
- Likely families: power/PCB/fuse, pump, fan/ignition sequence failure, low pressure (sensor/switch), gas supply.
- Parts implicated only after proving supply & demand: PCB, pump, fan, pressure sensor.

### Heating works, NO hot water (combi)
- Does the boiler *register* a DHW demand when a hot tap opens?
  - No demand registered → DHW flow sensor/turbine, its filter, harness.
  - Demand registered, boiler fires, water lukewarm → plate heat exchanger scaled/blocked, DHW thermistor, diverter not travelling fully.
  - Demand registered, boiler doesn't fire → diverter motor, PCB input, thermistor out of range.
- Classic: diverter valve cartridge/motor family. Confirm which sub-part before ordering (body / cartridge kit / motor).

### Hot water works, NO heating
- Checks: room thermostat/timer/receiver calling? Zone valves (system boilers)? Diverter stuck in DHW position (combi)? Pump/valves to heating circuit?
- Likely: external controls first (not a boiler spare), diverter stuck, zone valve motor on system installs.

### Ignition failure / lockout (boiler tries, then stops, reset needed)
- Sequence question: fan runs? Spark clicks? Flame lights at all? Lights then drops in seconds?
- Checks (user level, per user guides): gas on at meter, other gas appliances, prepayment credit, frozen/blocked condensate outside, flue terminal visibly blocked. Reset once only.
- Engineer families: ignition electrode/lead, gas valve (Gas Safe only), rectification probe + earth, condensate trap blocked internally, fan/APS proving, PCB.
- Verified anchors: Vaillant **F.28/F.29**, Ideal **L02/F2**, Worcester **EA**, Baxi-family **E133** — all mean "flame not detected/proven", none of them means "replace part X" on its own.

### Low pressure / keeps losing pressure
- User: re-pressurise to the user-guide figure (commonly 1–1.5 bar cold) via filling loop; bleed radiators, re-check.
- If pressure falls repeatedly: leak on system, expansion vessel flat/split (pressure swings high hot / low cold, PRV discharging), PRV passing after lifting, pressure sensor lying vs gauge.
- Parts: vessel, PRV, sensor, gauge — diagnose the *cause* of loss, don't just sell a sensor for a leaking system.

### DHW temperature swings / goes cold mid-shower
- Plate heat exchanger scale/blockage, DHW thermistor, flow sensor hunting at low flow, combi undersized/too-high flow. Check flow rate and inlet filter first.

### Noisy boiler
- Kettling (rumbling): scale/sludge in main exchanger, poor circulation, pump speed. Banging on ignition: delayed ignition — engineer. Whining: fan bearings or pump. Gurgling: air or condensate.

### Leaks from boiler
- Identify fluid & point: condensate (clear, from trap/pipe), primary water (from pump/AAV/PRV/valve joints, often rusty), DHW. Dye/corrosion trails point uphill to source. Order seals with the part.

### Intermittent / cold-weather only
- Frozen condensate (very common), APS tubes/flue wind effects on older boilers, sticking fan, marginal rectification (dirty probe/poor earth), low gas pressure at peak demand (engineer/supplier issue, not a spare).

## By brand fault-code system (verified examples only)

> Full tables live in each model's installation & servicing instructions. These anchors show the *system*, so counter staff recognise what they're being quoted.

### Baxi / Main / Potterton (BDR Thermea) — E-codes
Official list: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/technical-support/error-codes
- **E110** overheat (primary water/flue) · **E119** low pressure · **E133** ignition/flame/gas supply. Source: Baxi FAQ cited in brands file.
- Flag: the same E-number can carry different detail across ranges/generations — `check manual for that range`.

### Vaillant / Glow-worm family — F. codes
Official list: https://www.vaillant.co.uk/service/boiler-fault-codes/ and ecoTEC pro manual (PDF cited in brands file).
- **F.28** ignition unsuccessful (6+ listed causes incl. condensate, ignition, ionisation, earth, electronics) · **F.29** flame lost in operation · **F.32** fan · **F.61/F.62** gas valve actuation/shut-off delay · **F.64** flow/return NTC short · **F.75** no pressure rise at pump start (sensor/pump/air/low pressure).
- Flag: F.75 is the textbook "code ≠ one part" example — four different causes in Vaillant's own list.

### Ideal — F and L codes (Logic family presentation varies)
Official: https://idealheating.com/support/faqs/boiler-fault-codes ; Logic System2 user guide.
- **F01** low pressure · **F02** flame loss · **F03** fan · **F04/F05** flow/return thermistor · **F09** unconfigured PCB / gas valve short (as listed) · **L01** overheat/no flow · **L02** ignition lockout · **L06** false flame.
- Flag: older Logic displays flash letter + number separately — get a photo/video of the display.

### Worcester Bosch — letter/number codes
Official manual example (Greenstar CDi) via literature search https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/support/literature ; Fault Finder app feature https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/installers-choice/trade-tips/fault-finder
- **EA** flame not detected · **C6** fan speed low · **E9** safety temp limiter · **F0** internal error · **F7/FA** flame sensed incorrectly · **Fd** reset pressed by mistake (i.e. not a fault at all).
- Flag: Worcester codes differ between Greenstar generations (CDi vs 4000/8000 etc.) — model first.

### Others (Keston, Intergas, Alpha, Ariston, Ferroli, Vokera, Viessmann, Heatline, Morco, Ravenheat, Biasi)
- No fault-code tables are reproduced here because none were verified from an official manual page in this trawl. Route: model manual (see brands file) → fault table. Viessmann fault messages are in the service instructions via ViBooks; Intergas codes in its service docs via https://intergasstore.co.uk/downloads . Anything quoted from a forum/blog for these brands: `unverified — check manual`.

## Rules for counter staff
1. Never convert a code into a single part on the phone. Say: "On that model that code covers X, Y, Z — your engineer will prove which; the parts for those are…"
2. Ask for: display photo, data-badge photo, and "what does it do from cold?" — those three answer most calls.
3. Sell the seals/kit the diagram pairs with the part (see part-number checklist).
4. PCB last, gas valve never on suspicion — both need engineer's test results.

## Round 2 additions — lessons tied to model tables
- **New-generation code trap:** Baxi Combi 2 uses A/H/E.xx codes (model file §1), Worcester 4000 uses numeric 2xx codes, CDi uses letters (EA). First question on any code call is now 'which generation?' — a code read without the model is worse than no code.
- **F.75 wording differs by manual:** Glow-worm Energy manual lists F.75 as 'Pressure switch defective'; Vaillant ecoTEC guidance lists sensor/pump/air/pressure. Same code string, different depth — quote the product manual in front of you (see forum F.75 system lesson in forums file).
- **Diverter proving (Ideal Logic forum-verified):** if manually pressing the diverter (engineer, actuator removed) restores DHW, the plate is likely fine; suspect actuator drive/valve travel. If DHW demand isn't registered at all, go flow sensor first (see DHW worked examples: Ideal has separate flow/turbine and detection parts, Worcester lists Flow Sensor vs Flow Turbine Adaptor separately).
- **Manual flowchart > code table for Ideal:** Logic sends engineers through decision values (24Vdc at gas valve, 4 kΩ gas valve pins, 230VAC at fan — testing-values.md). Counter version: ask 'did they get voltage at the valve/fan?' before accepting a PCB order.
- **Intergas is the odd one out:** no diverter-based DHW switching on HRE combi in the usual sense, fault display is numeric on a temperature display (0-30), and its sensors are 12 kΩ (not 10 kΩ). Model file §7.


## Counter quick-reference — the 10 faults you're most likely to be asked about (Round 3)
Traceable to tables in model-fault-and-spares-tables.md / testing-values.md. 'First suspect' = most likely *family*, prove-it = the check that separates it. Gas Safe engineer does the proving.

| # | Customer says / code | First part/family to suspect | Check that proves it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "No heating, no hot water, code for low pressure" (Baxi E118-family/A.02.06, Ideal F1, Vaillant F.22, Worcester 1017) | Actually-low system pressure first — not a part | Gauge vs 1–1.5 bar cold (Alpha NX: 1–1.2); re-pressurise per user guide; if it keeps falling, leak/vessel/PRV — sensor only if gauge and display disagree |
| 2 | "It clicks, tries to light, locks out" (E133/133, F.28, 501, 227, L2) | Ignition/flame-proving family + condensate | Sequence stage reached; condensate frozen/blocked (cold snap first); engineer: >18 mbar at Ideal inlet, electrode condition, gas valve voltage (24Vdc Ideal) |
| 3 | "Hot water cold, heating fine" (combi) | Diverter travel / DHW demand sensing | Does boiler register DHW demand? No = flow sensor/turbine. Yes + fires = plate HEX/diverter travel. Engineer manually pressing diverter (Ideal forum-verified split) |
| 4 | "Heating fine, hot water goes cold mid-shower" | Plate heat exchanger scale/blockage | DHW temp/flow at tap vs boiler output; plate in/out temps; check DHW thermistor reading before condemning plate |
| 5 | Vaillant/Glow-worm F.75 | Water pressure sensor + pump + blockage as a system | Standing pressure, ~0.2 bar rise at pump start (forum), sensor zeroes when depressurised; hoses/filter blocked; ecoTEC plus may need F.75 service set on low-loss headers |
| 6 | "Pressure goes up to 3 when hot, drops when cold, water at outside pipe" | Expansion vessel (PRV is the victim) | Vessel air charge isolated/drained vs manual; water at Schrader = split diaphragm; only then PRV |
| 7 | "Boiler dead, blank display" | Power/fuse/PCB — in that order | Supply at boiler, board fuse, external controls; Vogue flowchart adds <185V mains check. PCB last |
| 8 | "Fan fault code" (F.32, F3, 160, 214/215) | Fan harness/supply before fan | Voltage arriving at fan (Ideal: 230VAC blue/brown present = fan, absent = PCB); fan free to spin, Hall/speed signal |
| 9 | "Overheat / kettling, locks out hot" (110, F.20, 224, L01) | Circulation: pump, air, sludge | Flow/return differential (Ideal/Vogue: >30°C flowchart branch), pump rotating freely, venting; thermistor resistance at temp (9.7–10.3kΩ @25°C Ideal/Keston) |
| 10 | "Works on heating, won't fire for hot water in summer" | DHW flow sensor/turbine or diverter stuck in CH | Demand icon on DHW draw; turbine spins/filter clean (Duo-tec servicing notes DHW filter & turbine clean); actuator movement on demand |

Rule printed under the counter: **code + model + data-badge photo before any part leaves the shelf.**

# Forums & Professional Resources — verified, with access limits

Access warning up front: good boiler-repair discussion is deliberately gated. Gas-side fault-finding shared with the public would be unsafe and, for paid work, Gas Safe is a legal requirement. Expect Gas Safe-verified areas to require a registration number; do not quote forum posts to customers as instructions.

## Verified resources

### UK Plumbers Forums — https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/
- Large UK trade/community forum. Verified structure: public plumbing/boiler advice areas plus a **Gas Safe Register-only area** (registration details required; forum threads discuss minimum requirements). Good for: real-world "this model does X" pattern recognition, which parts fail on which ranges, merchant/supplier experience.
- Use: search before asking; treat solutions as leads to verify in the manual, not as authority. Public posts vary in quality.

### National Gas Engineers — https://nationalgasengineers.co.uk/
- Positioned (per its site, found via search) as a learning app for UK gas engineers with trade forum / fault-code knowledge base for verified engineers. `Access/verification details unverified beyond its own homepage claims — check before recommending.`

### Gas Safe Register — https://www.gassaferegister.co.uk/
- Official register: check an engineer/business, gas safety guidance. Not a forum — the authority for "is this person legal for this appliance".

### Manufacturer technical support (often better than any forum)
- Baxi technical support + error codes: https://www.baxi.co.uk/professional/services/technical-support/error-codes (tech support hours Mon–Fri 8–6, Sat 8:30–2 per Baxi search result)
- Vaillant homeowner fault list / engineer booking line and installer literature@vaillant.co.uk (Literature Finder page): https://professional.vaillant.co.uk/for-installers/literature-finder/
- Worcester Fault Finder inside the Worcester Bosch professional app (enter code → meaning + spares link): https://www.worcester-bosch.co.uk/professional/installers-choice/trade-tips/fault-finder
- Ideal fault-code FAQ: https://idealheating.com/support/faqs/boiler-fault-codes
- DHS technical phone help 0330 123 3707 (parts identification, 7 days per FAQ): https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/frequently-asked-questions

## Not verified / use with care
- Generic fault-code blogs, YouTube teardowns, and retailer "what does code X mean" pages were deliberately **not** built into the fault tables. The recurring failure mode online is copying a code table from a different model generation. If a source doesn't name the exact model + manual edition, mark it `unverified — check manual`.
- Reddit / DIY forums: useful for "householder symptom wording" (how customers describe noises), never for gas-side procedure.

## Recurring diagnostic lessons (from official manuals/FAQs, not forum lore)
1. **Frozen/blocked condensate** is a manufacturer-listed ignition-failure cause (Vaillant F.28, Worcester EA guidance, Ideal L02 guidance) — first check in a cold snap, and the one check user guides allow householders.
2. **Low pressure** accounts for a large share of "boiler dead" calls (Baxi E119, Ideal F01, Vaillant F.75 family) — teach the filling-loop conversation.
3. **Codes with many causes** (Vaillant F.28 lists 6+, F.75 lists 4) are the norm; single-part answers online are a red flag.
4. **Earth/rectification faults** mimic gas valve/PCB failures: dirty ionisation probe or poor earth drops a lit flame in seconds.
5. **Air + sludge explain more "failed parts" than parts do**: F.75-type and overheat codes often clear with pressure/air/circulation sorted; pumps and sensors get condemned for system problems.
6. **The part that failed is often the victim**: PRVs pass because vessels fail; PCBs die because pumps/fans short. Sell the cause, not just the casualty.

## Round 2 additions — accessible forum threads actually read (19 Oct 2026)

### Vaillant ecoTEC F.75 thread — UK Plumbers Forums (public thread, fetched in full)
- Thread: https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/threads/vaillant-ecotec-f-75.94133/
- What engineers in the thread actually do: check standing pressure and whether the display shows ~**0.2 bar rise when the pump starts**; isolate/depressurise and see if the readout zeroes (if not, sensor is lying); check the filter behind the pressure sensor for blockage; check rubber hoses ('squeeze — if solid, replace', one poster upgrades to copper when renewing the pump); pump next; PCB 'only once'. One names the sensor: Vaillant 0020059717 (matches DHS Example 2 in dhs-lookup-worked-examples.md).
- Lesson for counter: F.75 = sensor + pump + blockage + hoses as a *system*. Selling just the sensor first is common, but warn it may be hoses/filter/pump. This matches Vaillant's own multi-cause manual list — forum and manual agree here.

### Ideal Logic 'No Hot Water' thread — UK Plumbers Forums (fetched in full)
- Thread: https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/threads/no-hot-water-fixed-and-broken-again-ideal-logic-24.132805/
- Story: DHW cold/barely warm (better when heating off/cold). Over time: flow cartridge, flow sensor, manifold, diverter cartridge + actuator changed, plate inspected 'very good' — fixed for 4 days, then failed again. Removing actuator and manually pressing the diverter restores hot water.
- Lessons: (1) manually moving the diverter proving DHW is a genuine diagnostic split (actuator/drive vs valve travel); (2) repeated part-swapping without finding why travel fails wastes money; (3) note the thread's moderation: first replies ask 'are you Gas Safe registered?' and limit help if not — public threads will often stop at the gas/combustion boundary. That gatekeeping is visible in the fetched thread, not assumed.

### Frozen condensate threads (search-indexed, not all fetched in full)
- 'Frozen condense' https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/threads/frozen-condense.15193/ ; 'Condense pipe frozen?' https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/threads/condense-pipe-frozen.101297/ ; 'Vokera condensing boiler — froze, thawed, now not working' https://ukplumbersforums.co.uk/threads/volkera-condensing-boiler-froze-thawed-now-not-working.15984/
- Recurring pattern (per search summaries — marked as summary-level, not full-thread verified): thaw external pipe, check trap, reset once; if water backed up, ignition/flame parts may have suffered — engineer. Consistent with manufacturer user-guide advice (round 1).

### Gas Safe-only areas — inaccessible, not summarised
UK Plumbers Forums' Gas Safe area and similar verified-engineer spaces require registration credentials I do not have. Their contents are **not** described here. Do not ask staff to relay credentials or scrape them.

# Legacy Boilers — still on repair rounds (Round 3, 19 Oct 2026)

Identification rule is doubled for legacy: many have had case/PCB swaps over 20+ years. **GC number + serial from the data plate is the only reliable key** — DHS appliance pages are organised exactly that way. Spares caution: listings mix current, superseded ('NOW USE …') and obsolete/no-replacement parts. Always read the product title in full.

## Potterton Suprima (30-100, L models) — heat-only, cast-iron era successor
- Verified GCs (search/DHS): Suprima 50 **41-607-77** (DHS page fetched, round 3 worked examples); range GCs 41-607-75 (30) to 41-607-82 (100) per trade listings — verify per output on badge.
- Typically fails: **PCB is the famous one** — DHS lists Potterton **5111603 Suprima PCB Kit 30-100** as the current kit (fetched on Suprima 50 page). Also on that page: gas valve 402550, fan 40958801, thermistor 404516, overheat thermostat 404517, electrode 407754.
- Caution: PCB kit is an *upgrade kit* (L models included in listings) — follow kit instructions; original single-board numbers may not order directly. Combustion-chamber insulation (5000537 front etc.) still listed — fragile on strip-down, order before opening.
- Source: https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/category/gas-boiler-uk/brand/potterton/appliance/potterton-suprima-50-pot338

## Potterton Profile / Prima, Baxi Solo — NOT deep-verified this round
- No manual/DHS page fetched for Profile/Prima/Solo in round 3. One verified sighting: 'Baxi 238295 Pilot Solenoid Solo 2 PF' appears as a cross-listed part on the DHS Suprima 50 page (fetched) — pilot-era Solo parts still catalogue-listed, but availability must be checked live per part.
- Route: DHS brand → Potterton/Baxi → exact model + GC. Do not claim typical-failure lists for these from memory. `unverified — check DHS/manual`.

## Ideal Classic (FF/RS, Mexico-era relatives)
- Round 1 verified DHS example (Ideal Classic FF 350, GC 41-391-96) with fan 171461, gas valve 171441, electrode 171442 etc. — see part-number-identification.md. Classic is the poster child for GC importance: FF/RS/SE/NF variants share names, parts differ (fan kits split 30-80 vs 30-60 on that page).
- Typical legacy pattern (from that fetched listing only): fans, gas valves, ignition electrodes, limits/thermostats and casing seals dominate the listing — heat-only, so no diverter/plate faults; DHW complaints on a Classic install are system/cylinder-side, not boiler spares.

## Worcester 24i/28i Junior & Greenstar CDi classic
- Round 3/2 verified DHS: Greenstar 28i Junior FSN NG **GC 47-311-87**, 267 parts listed (search) — fan 8716118443, electrodes 87161163810, flow sensor 8716122562 on fetched page (round 2 worked examples).
- CDi classic uses **letter codes (EA etc.)** — round 1 official manual extraction. The numeric 2000/4000/8000 system (round 3 §18/19) must not be applied to CDi/Junior-era boilers, and vice versa.
- Caution: Junior/CDi parts numbers are long Bosch numbers with generation splits (FSN suffix matters — it denotes a variant on the DHS appliance name itself).

## Vaillant TurboMAX / CombiCompact (VCW, 1988-95 era)
- Verified: CombiCompact VCW 282 E (88-95) **GC 47-044-18**, DHS page fetched round 3 (worked examples) with sub-diagrams including **Water Valve (to 04/95) vs (from 05/95)** — build-date split inside one model name.
- Obsolete evidence (search-verified, Heating Spare Parts listings): Vaillant 082745 listed 'OBSOLETE gas shut-off valve', 075549 'OBSOLETE covering plate' for this era — i.e. some parts are genuinely NLA; a DHS listing existing does not guarantee supply. Check live and prepare the customer for obsolete outcomes on gas-section parts.
- TurboMAX spare catalogue exists as a manufacturer document (heatingspares host, search-listed) — use via Vaillant/DHS cross-check, `host flagged`.

## Glow-worm CXi / HXi / Ultimate (pre-Energy)
- Verified DHS CXi 38 **GC 47-047-27** (fetched): PCB **2000802731** 'XI Range PCB Replacement' (also HXI/SXI), fan 801645, thermistor 801722, electrode kit 0020152564, pressure sensor S5720500 (Saunier Duval cross-listing — Vaillant-group sibling brand appearing in Glow-worm listings is normal here).
- **Supersession examples verified in search:** Glow-worm 801673 disconnector 'NOW USE 2000802600 filling loop'; 2000802658 interface card 'NOW USE 0020027897'. And a no-replacement example: S210188 rear combustion insulation listed with no known replacement (search summary) — obsolete can mean fabricate-or-condemn discussions for the engineer, not a counter sale.
- Ultimate (original/CXi-era): manuals via Glow-worm legacy page (round 1); Ultimate3 is the current generation (model file §23) — do not mix.

## Ferroli DOMI / older Modena-era
- Modena HE fault system is in model file §10 (round 2). DOMIproject/DOMIcondens generation: **no manual fetched round 3** — route Ferroli documentation (round 1) / DHS by GC. Ferroli legacy support in the UK has historically been thinner than Baxi/Vaillant — set delivery expectations only after a live DHS check. `typical failures unverified — do not quote from memory`.

## General legacy rules (all verified by examples above)
1. GC first, always — outputs/variants multiply (Suprima 30-100 = 7 GCs).
2. Read 'NOW USE', 'OBSOLETE', build-date splits (to/from month-year) on every listing.
3. Insulation/seals on strip-down: order the fragile bits (Suprima insulation, CXi door seal 801635) *with* the main part.
4. Heat-only legacy boilers (Suprima, Classic, Solo, Profile) have no combi hydraulics — route DHW faults to system parts.
5. If a gas-section part is NLA, that is an engineer/manufacturer conversation about appliance future — counter should flag early, not keep ordering alternatives.

# Model Fault-Code & Spares Tables — Round 2 (19 Oct 2026)

Fetched/parsed 19 Oct 2026 (Europe/London). Sources are the official installation/service manual PDFs below unless stated. Where a manual could not be fetched/parsed, that is said — do not fill the gap from memory. Gas Safe note from README applies throughout: these tables are for parts identification, engineer work is Gas Safe.

# Part-Number Identification — get the exact spare, first time

## The identity pack (collect ALL of this before searching)
- [ ] Photo of **data badge**: make, full model, kW output, **GC number (00-000-00)**, serial number, fuel type
- [ ] Boiler type: combi / system / heat-only; open-vent or sealed
- [ ] Fault code photographed + symptom in plain words + "what stage does it reach?"
- [ ] Engineer's test result that condemns the part (not just the code)

## Step-by-step method
1. **GC number first.** It pins the exact appliance variant. Search DHS Spares Finder / PartsArena by GC where possible — DHS appliance pages print the GC and only list parts for that appliance (verified example below). GC format/source: https://myboiler.com/what-is-a-gc-number/
2. **Open the exploded diagram for that appliance** (manufacturer spare parts manual, PartsArena, Viessmann Spare Parts App, DHS appliance page). Find the component visually — position matters because similar parts sit side by side (flow vs return NTC; diverter body vs motor).
3. **Diagram position → manufacturer part number.** Record both, plus diagram number/edition. Superseded numbers: manufacturer lists and DHS product pages show "fits / replaces" relationships — if a number has been superseded, order the current number and note the old one it replaces. `Never merge two numbers without a stated supersession source.`
4. **Variant checks before ordering:**
   - NG vs LPG (injectors, gas valves, restrictors, some burners)
   - Voltage / connector variant (fans, pumps, motors differ by generation)
   - Output variant (24/30/35kW models in one range often use different fans/gas valves/exchangers)
   - Left/right hand, flow/return, inlet/outlet size on hydraulics
   - **Seals included or not?** Check kit contents on the diagram/product page vs the separate O-ring/gasket position numbers. Order the seal kit the same visit.
   - Kit vs single part: many modern spares are kits (e.g. "Fan Assembly Kit") — check what's in the kit before also ordering its components separately.
   - PCB configuration: some replacement PCBs need setting up for the appliance (Ideal F09 = unconfigured PCB in Logic guidance); check manual notes so the engineer expects to configure it.
   - Genuine vs alternative/refurbished: DHS labels these options; for gas/combustion parts prefer genuine (see README/Baxi liability note).
5. **Cross-check in a second source** (manufacturer list vs DHS vs PartsArena). If two sources give different numbers for the same position — stop, phone manufacturer tech or DHS (0330 123 3707) with GC + serial.
6. **Write the full identity on the order**: make, model, GC, serial, part number, diagram position, fuel. This is what saves the return trip when a range spans 15 years of variants.

## Worked example (verified from a live DHS appliance page, 19 Oct 2026)
- Appliance page: Ideal Classic FF 350 — DHS states **GC Number: 41-391-96** for it.
- The page lists, for that appliance, e.g. "Ideal 171461 Fan Assembly Kit - Classic FF 30-80", "Ideal 171441 Gas Valve Kit", "Ideal 079662 Manifold Gasket Set" with the manufacturer part number first in each description.
- Source: https://www.dhsspares.co.uk/category/gas-boiler-uk/brand/ideal-domestic/appliance/ideal-classic-ff-350-ide226
- Lesson to copy (not the numbers — the *method*): GC pinned the appliance; manufacturer numbers came from the appliance-specific list; note how two different fan kits appear for different output sub-ranges (FF 30-80 vs FF 30-60 listings) — output variant check, step 4, is not optional.
- Do not copy prices/stock from that page into quotes — they are live.

## Second worked example — old catalogue on the box
- `/workspace/vaillant/sp.pdf` is Vaillant's spare parts catalogue 0020010870.05 (GB 10/2008) for ecoTEC plus 824/831/837 & 612–637, organised by exploded sections (04 Burner, 06 Heat exchanger, 08 Casing…).
- Use it to learn diagram layout only. A 2008 catalogue number **must** be checked for supersession in the current Literature Finder / DHS before ordering: https://professional.vaillant.co.uk/for-installers/literature-finder/

## Serial / date codes
- Formats are brand- and generation-specific. Worcester uses an FD factory-date code; Vaillant long serials encode production info — secondary explanation: https://www.trustapart.co.uk/how-old-is-my-boiler/ (`unverified against a manufacturer document — confirm with the manufacturer when age matters, e.g. warranty`).
- Safest practice: record serial verbatim, photograph it, and let the manufacturer/DHS decode it.

## Pre-order checklist (tape this to the counter)
```
[ ] Data badge photo (GC + serial legible)
[ ] Fault code photo + symptom + sequence stage
[ ] Diagram position AND manufacturer part number agree in 2 sources
[ ] Output / fuel / voltage variant checked
[ ] Supersession checked
[ ] Seals/gaskets for the job — included or added
[ ] Kit contents checked (not double-ordering kit components)
[ ] Genuine vs alternative stated to customer/engineer
[ ] Full identity written on order notes
```
